claims.text: The initial material is a W–Cu composite containing W particles or interconnected W ligaments in a Cu matrix.
A hierarchical W–Cu microstructure can be created with aligned W ligaments.
The Cu matrix distribution can be optimized as part of the same microstructural intervention.
Aligning W ligaments and optimizing the Cu distribution will reduce phase separation.
Aligning W ligaments and optimizing the Cu distribution will reduce interfacial void formation.
The hierarchical microstructure will improve bonding between W ligaments and the Cu matrix.
Reduced phase separation, fewer interfacial voids, and improved interface bonding will enhance thermal conductivity.
The treated W–Cu composite will have 20% higher thermal conductivity than the untreated composite.
High-temperature, high-heat-flux, and irradiation environments are relevant to joints between W plasma-facing materials and Cu-based cooling components.
The proposed 20% conductivity improvement will apply under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions relevant to W/Cu-based joints.
The magnitude of the conductivity improvement may vary with processing conditions and the resulting microstructure.
Thermal conductivity and microstructure should be measured for treated and untreated W–Cu composites under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions.
The hypothesis is falsified if the treated composite's thermal conductivity is less than 15% above that of the untreated composite.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome is a 20% increase, but the hypothesis is only falsified below 15%. An observed increase from 15% to less than 20% would fail the stated prediction without meeting the stated falsification criterion.
